Do you have a.mixed species see pack? I have about an acre to plant. What's the sowing rate? Thanks 
 

 Julian Katz

Hi Julian,

First off, I'm sorry it took this long to get back to you. A very intense stretch on our end is no excuse for leaving your question sitting, and we'll do better going forward. If planting an acre is still on your radar, here's what I'd suggest.

We don't currently have a pre-mixed multi-species pack, but it's easy to put one together from our individual seed packets, and honestly, for an acre that's probably the better route since you can pick the species mix that suits your land.

For an acre, the main species worth considering:

- Syriaca (common milkweed): spreads aggressively, great for large open areas, very hardy
- Incarnata (swamp milkweed): less spreading, tolerates wet and dry soil, easier to manage
- Tuberosa (butterfly milkweed): stays compact, great pollinator magnet, drier soils
- Speciosa (showy milkweed): similar to syriaca but a bit more restrained

For sowing rate, a rough guide is about 1 seed packet (70 seeds) per 10 to 15 sq ft if you're planting in clusters, or you can spread more thinly across a larger area and let them naturalize over a couple of seasons. For a full acre, you'd be looking at dozens of packets, depending on how densely you want coverage in year one versus letting it fill in over time.

All our seed options are here: https://lasclay.com/en/products/milkweed-seeds

If you tell me more about the site, sun exposure, soil type, and whether you want dense coverage right away or a more gradual spread, I can help you nail down quantities.

Warmly,
__
 Gabriel Gouveia 
Co-founder
Lasclay.com
